items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I am proud to say that I got to know him so well that me and my wife met him and his wife Lucille quite often whenever they came to Paris.

ctx.x: I dont remember who was in Lou Russell's band when they played at the Savoy on Easter Monday 1929 with us and the Royal Flush orchestra of Fess Williams but he was advertised to play two nights with Louis Armstrong. Russell's first name was Luis but the Savoy had him billed as Lou. Armstrong was being called Satchelmouth now and this was the first time he was coming to New York since he had left Fletcher Henderson. I was still in Cincinnati when that happened and as Armstrong was not with Fletcher when he came to…

of being able to see and hear my idol for the first time. That night, I went quite early to the Savoy because I did not want to miss a note coming from the horn of Satchel. There was a trumpet player with him whom I had met named Louis Metcalf. Metcalf sat on a high stool, wore a cardboard gold crown and called himself 'King Louis'! He had on his crown when Armstrong came on the stand after a big announcement by Buchanan. From the moment that he started the first number until the end of it, Russell's band sounded…

When Satchelmouth came on the stand I was pleasantly surprised because he was a much better looking man than the few bad photos I had seen and collected of him. He was not as fat as I thought he would be but he was stocky and not as dark as the photos had me believing. His trumpet looked like the most beautiful golden horn that I had ever seen. The more he played, the better he sounded and he was not playing the things he had recorded in the same manner that I had heard them. They were sounding better and much…
